messages.author: a413e6cf6c4ea2cc
messages.subject: Re: MethyKit
parts:
Hi Luke,

Yes, I am still maintaining methylKit together with Altuna Akalin.
Usually the best way to seek help would be via e-mail to methylkit_...@googlegroups.com or post a question using the web interface. 
For bugs and errors please open issues on the github issue tracker.

As you realized the unite function is meant to merge at least two samples and does not work with fewer. However if the information that you need is the chr ID, start, end and the methylation percentage, this you might aswell extract and calculate directly from the methylRaw object ('myobj'). You can extract the underlying data of an object using the ˋgetDataˋ function, this should give you a data.frame with chromosome ID, start, end, strand, coverage, numCs (#cytosines) and numTs (#thymines). Then you can simply calculate methylation percentage as #cytosines/(#cytosines + #thymines ).

Best,
Alex
 

Luke William Gent <LWG...@uclan.ac.uk> schrieb am Mi., 29. März 2023, 12:51:
Hi! 

Are you still the maintainer for MethylKit? If so I have an query I'd like to put forward, apologies if this is not the right way to do it! 

Prior to running a sequencing pilot experiment, I sequenced one (yes just one) sample on the MiSeq, the data was sent to colleague, of whom processed it and provided me with a .bam file. Now I don't really do any analysis in the linux terminal, hence why I was happy to know of MethylKit! As I want to get methylation information from this .Bam file. 

I got up to the steps of creating a MethylSet object via methRead(), however from there the tutorial suggests to create the 'meth' object that further downstream analysis is conducted on, I need to do 'meth=unite(myobj, destrand=FALSE)'; now I understand this is for aggregating multiple samples in the BAM file together so one can do DM analysis and such. Of course since mine is one sample, this function did not work correctly as it said 'uniting...Error in (function (cond)  :   error in evaluating the argument 'x' in selecting a method for function 'getData': subscript out of bounds'. 

Again, I believe I understand why. The trouble is, the part I want to get to which is to have the chr ID, start, end and the methylation percentage or beta value from my 'myobj'. However, I'm not sure how to get to that point considering I cannot create the 'meth' object. 

Please let me know if there is anything I can do. Also please let me know if this was too inappropriate to ask! 

Best,

Luke Gent


PhD R​esearcher in Forensic Science, 
Department of Natural Sciences
Member of @Forens-OMICS Team, University of Central Lancashire.

messages.author: a413e6cf6c4ea2cc
messages.subject: Re: MethyKit
parts:
Hi Luke,

If you are asking whether the coverage could be directly used in the calculations, then yes, it is basically the sum of cytosines and thymines.

If you want to know whether you should filter for a minimum coverage to include a certain base, then yes, we usually require egh single base to have a coverage of at least 10 reads to be kept.

I hope this answers your questions.

Best,
Alex
